name: Grid Agent
description: Something that stands on tiles and steps between them. It is deliberately not movement.character_body: a character body is a box in continuous space that gravity acts on and that can be anywhere, and an agent on a grid is on a tile or it is not. The difference is not cosmetic — a tile can be OCCUPIED, which is what lets one unit block another, what makes a footprint mean something, and what a turn can be taken in. The two are alternatives, not layers, and a build that has both wants two different things from the same word.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application (generator/iso/GridAgent.ts); not verifiable from this repository.
The 3D runtime moves a character body through continuous space.

inputs.name: footprintWidth
inputs.description: Tiles occupied along x. A footprint larger than one tile is why occupancy is stored per tile rather than as a single position.

inputs.name: maxStepUp
inputs.description: Elevation levels this agent can climb in one step. The single most consequential number here: it decides which parts of a map are reachable at all, and it is easy to leave at a value that fences an agent into the flat patch it spawned on.

inputs.name: maxStepDown
inputs.description: Levels this agent can drop in one step. Deliberately larger than maxStepUp by default, because falling is easier than climbing — which makes reachability ASYMMETRIC. An agent can walk down into ground it cannot walk back out of, and any build that lets a player send a unit somewhere has to decide whether that is a trap or a feature.

inputs.name: blocksOthers
inputs.description: Whether this agent's tiles are impassable to other agents. False is what a ghost, a projectile, or an overlapping crowd wants.
